dimensions.explanation: The reading concerns material post-authorisation changes to investment objectives, policies or restrictions of the circular's defined UCITS funds. It does not extend the exemption to every fund described elsewhere as UCITS or to initial authorisation.

Covered funds are UCITS domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland or the Netherlands, and UK-domiciled collective investment schemes authorised as UK UCITS. Materiality, novelty, complexity and possible local policy implications are not defined in the supplied text and require case-specific judgment.

Relief requires compliance with home-jurisdiction requirements. Either novel or complex product features, or possible local policy implications, excludes relief. Pre-effective-date applications still awaiting approval or authorisation remain under the existing process.

The circular removes a prior-approval requirement conditionally; it does not grant approval, establish licence possession or certify overall compliance. The exceptions preserve prior approval for the described investment changes. Failure of the home-requirements condition establishes no entitlement to this exemption, rather than a means of curing home non-compliance through SFC approval. Notifications and SFC post-vetting remain separate.

The express Effective Date is 2025-11-28, which controls the introductory reference to immediate effect. 'Before' excludes applications received on that date. The proposed transition reading assesses outstanding approval or authorisation at commencement; the text does not expressly specify that assessment instant or address withdrawal and resubmission.

The relevant FAQs, forms and checklists, existing approval process, applicable home-jurisdiction requirements and facts of the proposed change are needed for a final application. citations.quote: Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC.

readings.distinction: The result answers: 'Does this change qualify for the circular's removal of prior SFC approval?' It is an exemption-eligibility predicate, not an overall compliance decision. Within scope, true means the stated exemption applies; false means one or more conditions for this exemption fail. False alone does not establish every requirement under the unavailable existing process. Outside scope, the result supplies no conclusion.

readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] A material post-authorisation investment change qualifies for removal of prior SFC approval from 2025-11-28 if the fund meets the circular's UCITS definition, the change complies with home-jurisdiction requirements, it involves neither novel nor complex product features, it has no possible local policy implications, and it is not covered by the preserved process for outstanding applications received before that date. True means those exemption conditions are satisfied; false means this exemption is unavailable. Thus materiality alone does not require prior approval. The product-feature and local-policy exceptions retain prior approval, while home non-compliance prevents reliance on the exemption. A pending pre-effective-date application continues through the existing process, whose detailed requirements are absent. Fund management companies must still address applicable notifications and filings; the SFC retains post-vetting, enquiry and regulatory-action powers. No particular fund or change can be classified on the supplied facts.
readings.subject: Eligibility for removal of prior SFC approval for material UCITS investment changes
